answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal deadline create severe constraint. Switching vendors or adding second source at 94% line utilization introduces delivery risk we cannot absorb. Deferral is impossible—contract expires without auto-renew. Verification of memory_c4 (successful prior renegotiation) de-risks the negotiate_terms path: if benchmarking recovered margin before, targeted renegotiation on price and terms can credibly address the 18% mandate while keeping incumbent relationship and integration stable (memory_c1, memory_c6 show stability value). The incumbent's history of accurate invoicing and volume pricing optionality (memory_c2, memory_c6) means negotiated renewal carries lower execution risk than vendor switch under timeline pressure. Uncertainty is preserved because: (1) we do not know if 18% is achievable in 14 days without fallback, (2) market rates may have moved, (3) incumbent's flexibility is untested under this deadline. High delivery-risk flag reflects 94% utilization—any supply break cascades immediately. This is a guarded test of negotiation leverage, not a full commitment.
